1.Name: Tree-heart Fruit
1.Description: A plant variety brought in by a merchant from the Dark Forest. It's sweet, seedless, and feels soft and squishy in the mouth, plump and bursting with juices. Consuming too many of them can make you feel heaty.
1.LockedDes: Available in the Garden of Wonders.

2.Name: Lover's Pearls
2.Description: An edible orchid-like flower with fleshy petals. The plant comprises two parts, the twisting vines and the bulbous stamen resembling a pearl, hence its name.
2.LockedDes: Available in the Garden of Wonders.

3.Name: Ringtailed Viper meat
3.Description: Leafy Ringtailed Viper meat is firm and succulent. They are prized game as their habitat is extremely inaccessible.

4.Name: Scorpion Pincers
4.Description: Scorpion Pincers may be terrifying in appearance, it is actually non-poisonous. Once peeled, it is succulent with a refreshing taste that is great for removing gamey smells on meat.

5.Name: Oasis Grain spices
5.Description: A type of herbaceous plant found deep in the swamps. Upon being heated it releases a spicy, hot substance that stifles the nose. It is often used as a seasoning when cooking meat.

6.Name: Purple pumpkin
6.Description: A premium pumpkin with purple flesh, which tastes sublime after stewing. Their popularity means their prices soar during harvest season.

7.Name: Pure cowlpie milk
7.Description: Pure cowlpie stock is hard to find these days. Their milk is highly nutritious and therefore precious.

8.Name: Bell Whistles
8.Description: A succulent fruit found in the Dreamwood, they are sometimes mistaken for onions due to their purple color and multi-layered skin. However, they are more nutritious than onions.

9.Name: Blue-spine cod
9.Description: This is a ferocious, flesh-eating fish that dwells in the deep waters by the Hermit Isle. Its meat has a soft and fatty texture.

10.Name: Soul snatcher sauce
10.Description: Local to the Hermit Island, soul snatcher is commonly used as a spice. When dried in the sun, they emit a chilling and peculiar aroma. Improper handling when preparing a meal can lead to hallucinations.

11.Name: Short-tail Veal Steak
11.Description: Short-tail bovines are said to roam around the Steelthorn Cliffs, which they can climb up to make a hasty escape whenever they feel threatened.

12.Name: Steelthorn Hen
12.Description: Native to the Steelthorn Cliffs, the hen is fatty, juicy, and perfect for roasting.

13.Name: Chieftain's Peak Bok-choy
13.Description: Only Bok-choys that thrive on Chieftain's Peak can withstand hours of boiling.

14.Name: Lanternberry Jam
14.Description: A rare sweet jam with an enchanting glow. Sampling it directly would color your tongue in fluorescent blue.

15.Name: Oval Citrus
15.Description: A magically enhanced fruit with an exquisite aroma. They are quite precious as they are challenging to grow.

16.Name: Golden Apple
16.Description: Fruit of the oasis. Very sweet and juicy with a crunchy texture. Often made into jam.

17.Name: Twin Persimmons
17.Description: Wilders cultivated edible fruits and vegetables into one plant that produces two different persimmon varieties; one red and one yellow. The red possesses a robust sweet flavor and the yellow a slightly sour flavor.

18.Name: Succulent Dewdrop
18.Description: A vined plant that possesses a fragrant, mouth-watering aroma, it has a multitude of uses as an ingredient.

19.Name: Rock Orchid
19.Description: A prehistoric plant that grows on craggy rock faces, it only bursts through the rock's exterior under warm conditions. Its flowers, which are extremely rare, have luscious petals that can be squeezed into juice.

20.Name: Polar Snowmelt
20.Description: During the very first snowfall of the year, snow crystals fall on polar glaciers and are collected and stored in a special bottle. The snow melts into a premium snowdew.
